source.title: The Missing Curve Detectors of InceptionV1: Applying Sparse Autoencoders to InceptionV1 Early Vision

page_placements.theme: Feature granularity depends on the sparsity setting (L0/L1), not only width

record.file_problem: None noted; the text is readable, though one cross-reference appears as “??”.
record.tranche_reason: It varies the SAE L1 coefficient and reports how the features representing a double-curve neuron change; this is a different test from comparing dictionaries of increasing size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that one SAE represents mixed3b/n/359 with two single-curve features and a double-curve feature, and that increasing L1 reduces the double-curve feature’s maximum activation while increasing the single-curve features’ maxima. It does not compare dictionary sizes or establish that smaller-dictionary feature inputs are partitioned by larger-dictionary features. The plotted activation values are not transcribed in the text.
record.test_reason: The study does not test feature splitting as the claim defines it. Every version concerns how SAE latents change with dictionary size, or how latent families, absorption or the training objective behave. This paper instead shows one 8× SAE per layer decomposing polysemantic InceptionV1 neurons into more monosemantic features, which is superposition disentangling, not the splitting of coarse SAE features. Its one sweep varies the L1 coefficient for a single neuron's features and reports maximum activations, not latent firing, coverage, direction or splitting. That bears on sparsity-sensitivity of one decomposition, not on whether splitting is an artifact of the objective (V6), so it goes under fits_no_version. The record's T2/tests is not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs on InceptionV1 early vision reveal interpretable features invisible at the neuron level, including curve detectors that fill orientation gaps, and split some polysemantic neurons into more monosemantic features. They say SAEs look promising for CNNs. The L1 result is offered as evidence that the extra double-curve feature may be an SAE failure, but they present the work as an early, non-systematic report.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies SAEs to InceptionV1 image activations, including branch-specific SAEs, and varies L1 for a curve-feature example; it does not compare dictionary sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported double-curve and single-curve feature maximum activations change with the L1 coefficient.

fits_no_version.finding: In one 8× mixed3b SAE, neuron mixed3b/n/359 decomposes into two single-curve features plus a double-curve feature. Raising L1 (two higher values, unstated) lowers the double-curve feature's maximum activation and raises the single-curve features' maxima (Figure 3; figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a composite SAE feature coexists with its component features depends on the sparsity coefficient (sparsity-sensitivity of SAE decompositions in vision models).

fits_no_version.finding: The SAE decomposes the polysemantic neuron conv2d1/n/44 into several gradient, colour and Gabor features. It also decomposes mixed3b/n/376 into a generic boundary detector and a fur-specific boundary detector (Section 3.1; qualitative only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs decompose polysemantic CNN neurons into more monosemantic features, sometimes a generic and a specialised pair.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as a very early report and say they do not aim to defend the generality of the results systematically. The L1 comparison is one neuron example, and numerical activations and exact higher L1 values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly test the listed versions. The paper also reports curve-detector responses and branch specialization, but these do not test dictionary-size splitting, absorption, cross-size latent decomposition, or the causal interpretation in V6.

untested.parts: All of it: no dictionary-size sweep and no matching of features across sizes.
All of it: no language models or open SAE releases; the study is a vision CNN only.
All of it: no nested families or hierarchy analysis. The generic versus fur-specific boundary decomposition is anecdotal, from a single SAE.
All of it: no parent/child firing or absorption measurement.
All of it: no comparison of latents across SAE sizes.
All of it: no test that splitting comes from the objective, and no Matryoshka or other alternative objective. The L1 sweep concerns one neuron decomposition, not splitting.

record.verdict_notes: 'Split' in this paper means neuron-to-feature decomposition (superposition), not the dictionary-size feature splitting of Bricken et al. The record's V6 'supports' label is removed. The appendix on cross-branch superposition and branch specialisation is unrelated to any version.

versions.untested_parts: No dictionary-size sweep, matching of features across dictionary sizes, input-partition test, or directional-proximity measurement.
No test across large language models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families or a hierarchy of concepts.
No parent-child feature firing or absorption test, and no test of whether changing size or sparsity fixes absorption.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents and completeness.

The study varies L1 sparsity for one neuron’s curve-related features, but does not establish that splitting is an artifact that says little about the model’s own units, test correlated or hierarchical inputs as the cause, or evaluate Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: InceptionV1

conditions.value: Two coefficients higher than the default 3.5e-6; exact values not stated

rows.measure: Maximum activations of the analogous double-curve and left/right single-curve features
rows.baseline: Default L1 coefficient 3.5e-6; numerical baseline values not stated
rows.value: As L1 increased, the analogous double-curve feature’s maximum activation fell, while the left- and right-curve features’ maximum activations increased; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the trend across two additional SAEs; it does not state the two L1 values or numerical activations.
rows.check: The row measures maximum activations of double-curve and single-curve features across three L1 coefficients for one neuron (mixed3b/n/359). That is a neuron-to-feature decomposition, not a coarse SAE feature splitting into finer ones. It does not test V6's claim that splitting arises from the objective on correlated or hierarchical inputs, and no alternative objective is tested. The values are figure-only and the higher L1 values are not stated. Unlink it from V6.

relation.reason: It reports neurons 'split' into monosemantic SAE features, a related idea, but does not test feature splitting across dictionary sizes.

tranche.reason: The study decomposes InceptionV1 neurons into SAE features and varies L1 for one neuron. It never varies dictionary size or compares latents across SAE sizes. The double-curve and single-curve result is a composite-versus-component effect of sparsity, not parent and child splitting or absorption, so the study neither tests nor uses any version.

source_check.notes: The mixed3b SAEs are branch-specific (5x5 only). Appendix A says cross-branch superposition is significant, so these SAEs can hide features. The L1 sweep has three SAEs with unstated coefficients and only figure-level activations. Expansion factors run from 2x to 8x by layer; there is no dictionary-size sweep.

statements.correction: None needed. Optional detail: the SAE covers only the 5x5 branch of mixed3b. Two more SAEs with higher L1 were trained. Neither the L1 values nor the activation values are stated.
statements.problem: None. The text has mixed3b/n/359 decomposing 'primarily' into two monosemantic curve detectors and one double-curve detector. As L1 rises, the double-curve maximum falls and the left and right curve maxima rise. The 8x and mixed3b details are right.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Higher-L1 SAEs for the mixed3b/n/359 curve-feature decomposition
reader_labels.reason: The reported feature activations shift as L1 increases, with the double-curve feature weakening and the single-curve features strengthening (r1). This supports the tested claim that sparsity settings can change or reduce this decomposition, not the broader artifact interpretation.
